notes: SHIP v1.14.429 - ONE COLOUR VOCABULARY. THE FLAT ELEVATION STOPS RENDERING NINE DEVICE CLASSES GREY. WHAT WAS WRONG, AND FOR HOW LONG. rackElevation_buildHtml wrote the RAW master_hostType code straight into data-type - gpu, sw, pwr, patch, stor, cpu, server, cdu, fw, media, other - while the flat CSS is keyed on DISPLAY keys. Only two of the eleven codes intersected, so on every Master rack NINE device classes matched no rule at all and painted grey. This file has known it since v1.14.255, where the comment above _TMAP calls it a PRE-EXISTING elevation bug, NOT introduced here, owed its own ship. This is that ship. That comment says only gpu; it predates .245 adding a server return, so the honest count was 2 of 11 rather than 1 of 10 - measured here, not inherited. THE DOOR IS NOT A NEW TABLE. RACKENGINE-SPEC section 7 asks for Vocabulary.typeOf and reads as though it must be designed. It must not: the map already existed. _TMAP was hoisted to module scope in .255 for exactly this reason, one map two readers, so Vocabulary is a NAMED DOOR over tables that were already present and duplicates nothing. A second copy is the drift the .251 to .253 media saga is a written record of, and would have guaranteed a repeat the next time a colour was ruled. IDEMPOTENCY IS LOAD-BEARING. typeOf(typeOf('sw')) must be 'switch', not 'unknown'. A naive lookup with an unknown fallback returns unknown on the second pass, so any path normalising twice would silently ERASE a real device class. Safe because no _TMAP key is also a different key's value - the four codes appearing on both sides each map to themselves - so checking RAW first is unambiguous. Pinned three levels deep for all eleven codes. An unmapped code resolves to unknown, REAL GEAR WE COULD NOT CLASSIFY, and never to blank, which is a positive claim that the U is empty - that exact fallback once rendered 459 real SPARKS devices as blanking panels. THE COLOUR RULING. Three types genuinely disagreed between the 3D bay and the flat canvas: pdu was gold in 3D and GREEN in flat, storage pink in 3D and GOLD in flat, server light-blue in 3D and SLATE in flat. Section E of the INSPECT-3D port is explicit that the bay must never contradict the elevation, so routing blind would have replaced everything is grey with coloured and contradicting the bay. Owner ruled 2026-08-10: THE 3D BAY WINS. Values here are lifted from TYPE_COLOR, the tray's own table - not re-typed and not re-picked. The standing 2026-08-06 ruling is unchanged and honoured: patch, media and unknown STAY GREY, stated explicitly rather than left to fall through. Coverage goes 2 of 11 to 8 of 11. Text colour is part of the ruling rather than decoration: four of these backgrounds are light and the base server rule sets color white, which on #7fd0ff would be unreadable - dark ink on the light channels, white on violet. THE RULE 17 TRAP THIS SHIP HAD TO AVOID, AND IT IS SUBTLE. The base rack-canvas-block[data-type=...] rules are NOT house-scoped and paint under ?legacy=1 too. Changing the ATTRIBUTE VALUE changes what the legacy house MATCHES without touching one legacy rule: raw stor matches nothing and renders grey today, while normalised storage would hit the base rule and turn gold - a legacy behaviour change arrived at entirely through a redesign-house edit. So the normalisation is GATED on redesign_isOn, the same _fit the function already computes, and under legacy the raw code is emitted exactly as it always was. Both halves are pinned by test, in both directions. SCOPE HELD DELIBERATELY. RackEngine._resolve, the I8 data contract from the same held branch, is NOT included: nothing calls it, and shipping it here would be dead code. It belongs to the M2-b data-contract ship where it will actually be used. The scrubbar writer has the same shape and the same problem but is a different surface that was neither measured nor ruled, so it is left alone and recorded rather than swept in. The held branch itself was 63 commits stale and conflicted; these lines were rebuilt on current main rather than merged. TESTS: new spec 20-vocabulary, six tests - the full raw-to-display map, idempotence three levels deep, unmapped resolves to unknown and never blank, 8 of 11 codes paint and the three ruled-grey ones stay grey, and BOTH halves of the Rule 17 guard driven through the real rackElevation_buildHtml. 20 + 06-composition + 09-master-binding + 19: 26 passed. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces 4589/4589, CRLF 57055 with 0 bare LF, three-stamp lockstep. DEVICE-VERIFY: open a Master rack in the flat elevation. Devices that were grey should now carry their channel colour - GPU cyan, switch violet, PDU and CDU gold, storage pink, server and CPU light blue - and patch, media conv and unclassified gear stay grey on purpose. The 3D bay and the flat elevation must agree on every one.
